candidates.tagline: No driver, no problem — except when the problem is a lit firework.
candidates.story: On July 4, 2026, Waymo robotaxis drove directly into lit fireworks in San Francisco, gridlocked for hours as batteries ran out, and had to be towed — while the company's handful of remote operators couldn't unstick dozens of stalled cars at once.
candidates.why_funny: The car designed to remove human error drove into explosives because there was no human to say 'maybe don't.'
candidates.alt: Row of white Waymo autonomous robotaxis with sensor domes on their roofs, parked on a San Francisco city street

candidates.tagline: Apple scraps affordable Vision Pro — $3,499 ski goggles remain aspirational.
candidates.story: On July 8, 2026, Samsung cancelled display development for a cheaper Apple Vision Pro after Apple abandoned the project entirely, meaning there will never be a budget version of the headset that sold only ~600,000 units in two years at $3,499.
candidates.why_funny: Apple designed $3,499 ski goggles tethered to an external battery puck, flopped with fewer sales than a slow iPhone afternoon, then cancelled the plan to make them affordable.
candidates.alt: A conference attendee wearing an Apple Vision Pro headset — thick goggle-like device with an external cable attached — at a technology conference
